user.title: HA-BEMS
user.description: Create missing shared inputs, import existing forecast entities, or add a flexible-device management module. Inputs can be reused by multiple modules.

entity_creator.title: BEMS entity creator
entity_creator.description: Create entities you don't already have in Home Assistant. Modules can also use existing entities.

thermal_storage.title: Thermal storage management — coming soon
thermal_storage.description: Planned: local feed-forward MILP for domestic hot water and building heating, using tunable energy demand, electricity prices, PV availability and a simple COP. Domestic hot water runs first; heating respects its reserved heat-pump windows. No indoor-temperature feedback or historical model training is planned for this first thermal approach. Submit to return to the main menu.

soc.title: Battery seasonal SOC min threshold
soc.description: Create a monthly seasonal SOC threshold with twelve editable percentages. If you already have a threshold entity, select it directly in FBC setup instead.

monthly.title: Battery seasonal SOC min threshold
monthly.description:
January to December. Default values are editable suggestions based on Central European solar irradiation conditions. At or below this threshold, HA-BEMS plans to leave the battery in standard operation. For FBC, the planned charging limit equals the configured maximum charging power. Your Home Assistant automations apply the plan.

Electricity consumption varies unpredictably, and forecasts inevitably contain errors. This threshold acts as a safeguard: it reduces the flexibility available to HA-BEMS while lowering the risk of undesirable battery operation.

existing_entity.title: Battery seasonal SOC min threshold
existing_entity.description: Select an available sensor, number or input_number containing the active threshold from 0 to 100 with unit %. Its calendar logic stays with that entity. No automatic fallback is used if it becomes unavailable.

load_profile.title: Non-flexible load profile
load_profile.description:
Estimate the non-flexible behind-the-meter building demand at 15-minute resolution. Enter annual consumption excluding separately controlled flexible loads like heat pumps, EVs, etc. Modelling is based on standard load profiles: choose H0, H25 or a constant profile throughout the year. H25 contains some average PV self-consumption influence. Select the public holiday calendar here, then choose a Bundesland or National holidays only in the next step. All fields can be changed later.

Sources: [H0 — VDEW 1999/2000 profile tables (ZIP)](https://www.bdew.de/media/documents/Profile.zip); [H25 — BDEW 2025 profile tables (XLSX)](https://www.bdew.de/media/documents/Kopie_von_Repr%C3%A4sentative_Profile_BDEW_H25_G25_L25_P25_S25_Ver%C3%B6ffentlichung.xlsx). [BDEW background and application notes](https://www.bdew.de/energie/standardlastprofile-strom/).

fbc.title: Electrical storage management — FBC
fbc.description: FBC (Forecast based charging) provides operating plans and recommendations. Optionally consider predicted building demand by selecting a generated or imported load forecast in the next step. Each virtual device includes an FBC charging limitation enabled switch: off publishes maximum charging power for the complete plan. Use your own Home Assistant automations to apply the results to your battery system.

data.name: Virtual device
data.soc_entity: Select actual battery SOC in % used by the FBC algorithm
data.seasonal_soc_entity: Battery seasonal SOC min threshold entity

data_description.name: Name of the virtual Battery control strategy device; this does not rename your physical battery.
data_description.soc_entity: Select the measured battery state of charge, with unit % and a value from 0 to 100.
data_description.seasonal_soc_entity: If you don't already have this entity, create it using HA-BEMS: BEMS entity creator → Battery seasonal SOC min threshold.

fbc_battery.title: Battery parameters
fbc_battery.description: Use the usable (net) battery capacity corresponding to the selected SOC sensor's full 0–100% range. The efficiency is one constant factor converting forecast PV energy into stored battery energy (for example 0.95). Include the combined conversion and charging losses once. At or below the seasonal minimum SOC, the complete FBC plan allows maximum charging power.

data_description.charge_efficiency: Factor from 0 to 1: 0.95 means that 95% of forecast PV energy becomes stored battery energy. A constant factor cannot recover PV peaks already clipped in the forecast.
data_description.capacity_kwh: Enter the usable energy in kWh corresponding to a change from 0% to 100% on the selected battery SOC sensor.
data_description.target_soc_percent: SOC that FBC aims to reach by the end of the day. Keep this value aligned with the maximum SOC configured in your battery system.
data_description.max_charge_power_w: Maximum charging power supported by your battery system, in W. Also used as the output limit.

fbc_forecast.title: Select FBC forecast inputs
fbc_forecast.description:
Select a PV forecast registered under BEMS entity importer. Optionally select an existing HA-BEMS non-flexible load profile or a building load forecast registered in the importer. Without load, FBC uses PV generation only. With load, FBC uses max(0, PV generation minus building demand), assuming AC PV generation without unaccounted inverter clipping. Inputs must cover at least the next 72 hours at 15-minute resolution. A selected load input must be valid; FBC will not silently revert to PV only.

{reason}

data_description.load_forecast_input: Choose None for unchanged PV-only behaviour. For load-aware FBC, use building demand before PV/battery balancing; exclude battery charging. Demand above PV becomes zero available surplus; predicted battery discharge is not simulated.

fbc_preview.title: FBC forecast input tests passed

entity_importer.title: BEMS entity importer
entity_importer.description: Register existing forecast entities as shared inputs. HA-BEMS tests their format and coverage, and exposes an input status. Modules reuse the same validated input.

menu_options.future_imports: Electricity prices and additional forecasts — coming soon

future_imports.title: Additional forecast inputs — coming soon
future_imports.description: Planned input types: electricity import prices, electricity export prices and further forecasts needed by future modules. Each type will have a documented unit and value format. Price inputs are not implemented in this version. Submit to return to the importer menu.

import_pv.title: Import PV generation forecast
import_pv.description:
Select one forecast sensor prepared in Home Assistant. Its state must be nonnegative power in W. Required attributes: schema_version: 1, source_updated_at (original source update time with timezone), and forecast (ordered list of start, end and power_w records). Each record must contain a timezone-aware start/end and the interval-average power in W for exactly 15 minutes. Include the current quarter-hour and at least the next 72 hours without gaps, including explicit nighttime zeros. Never replace missing data with zero. A rolling helper normally needs 289 intervals. HA-BEMS tests the format and coverage before registering this input for reuse by modules. Source age is informational and does not reject an input. The original forecast remains on your source entity; the importer adds a status sensor without duplicating the forecast. [Helper design and example]({helper_docs_url}).

{reason}

data_description.forecast_entity: Use a prepared helper such as sensor.pv_generation_forecast_72h. Provider sensors must first be converted to the documented shared format.

import_preview.title: Forecast input test passed

load_region.title: Non-flexible load profile — holiday region
load_region.description: Choose the Bundesland for the selected country, or National holidays only. Regional public holidays use the Sunday load profile. This setting can be changed later.

import_load.title: Import building load forecast
import_load.description:
Select a prepared building demand forecast sensor, before PV/battery balancing and excluding battery charging. Its state must be finite nonnegative interval-average power in W. Required attributes: integer schema_version: 1, source_updated_at (original source update timestamp with timezone), and forecast (a native list of start, end and power_w records). Include the current quarter-hour and at least the next 72 hours in ordered, contiguous 15-minute intervals. Never replace missing consumption data with zero. A rolling helper normally needs 289 intervals. Setup tests the format and coverage; source age is information only. The importer exposes input health and keeps the forecast on your source entity. Existing HA-BEMS load profiles can be selected directly in FBC without importing them. [Helper format and AI prompt]({helper_docs_url}).

{reason}

data_description.forecast_entity: Select a forecast of building consumption, not net grid import, measured consumption history or an energy total in kWh.

error.invalid_entity: Choose an available numeric percentage entity from 0 to 100 with unit %.
error.self_reference: Choose an external entity; this entry cannot use its own output as its input.
error.invalid_load_profile: Check the annual consumption and the holiday country/region combination.
error.invalid_forecast: Forecast test failed. Correct the imported input or its source using the detailed message below; setup cannot continue until the test passes.
error.no_pv_import: No PV input is registered yet. Add HA-BEMS again, choose BEMS entity importer → PV generation forecast, and complete its test before setting up FBC.
